copies.headline: Noah's Best Roster Yet Meets Kaleb's Kicker Problem
copies.body:
Kaleb holds thin edges almost everywhere — Goff by one over Maye, Jeanty and a doubtful Breece Hall by five at running back, Fannin by two at tight end — and then hands it all back with Harrison Butker projected for zero. That's a self-inflicted wound you don't recover from in a game decided by single digits, and the Hall tag makes it worse: RJ Harvey at 11 is the fallback, and Jeanty is a 3.5-point road dog in a 45.5 game. McConkey and Allen are both questionable too, which turns a deep receiver room into a guessing game.
Noah's path is the Arizona-Detroit track meet. Michael Wilson at 17 in a 54.5-total game Arizona is losing by a touchdown is exactly the chase script he needs, and James Cook in Buffalo-Rams gives him a second shootout. Garrett Wilson in a 39.5 game is the drag.

copies.headline: CJ's Receivers Can't Cover Two Tight Ends
copies.body:
The margin lives at tight end and receiver, where John is up nine at each spot. Trey McBride in a 54.5-total game with Arizona chasing Detroit is exactly the script that gets him 12 targets, and Brock Bowers on the bench as a 19-point tight end is a luxury CJ can't answer — Brenton Strange is his ceiling. The receiver gap is worse than nine points if Rashee Rice's questionable tag turns red, because then CJ is starting Parker Washington, Devaughn Vele and Emeka Egbuka and hoping. John's Rams stack of Stafford, Kyren Williams and Puka Nacua against Buffalo in a 54.5 shootout is the highest-leverage group on either side.
CJ's path is the backfield, and it's real: Jonathan Taylor at Pittsburgh plus Judkins, with Ollie Gordon and TreVeyon Henderson behind them. That's four usable backs to John's two-and-a-half. But a two-point running back edge and a two-point quarterback edge don't cover eighteen points of pass catchers, and CJ's 3-1 is already carrying +0.8 wins of luck.

copies.headline: Isaac's Backfield Outruns Grant's Thin Depth
copies.body:
Two teams in the 9-10 range of the power rankings, both 2-2 with all-play records under 37 percent, both quietly getting away with it. The separator is running back. Javonte Williams is home with Dallas favored by 8.5 in a 47.5-total game, the exact script where a lead gets ground out, and Jaylen Warren adds another ten-plus against Indianapolis. Grant counters with Tony Pollard in a 37.5-total game where Tennessee is getting 7.5, and Omarion Hampton. Behind that it's Jacory Croskey-Merritt and an Austin Ekeler projected for four, with two backs already on IR. That's not depth, that's a hope.
Grant's edge is Amon-Ra St. Brown in the 54.5-point Detroit-Arizona game, plus Jacoby Brissett throwing from behind in the same shootout — real ceiling. But Isaac's receiver room is deeper even if Ja'Marr Chase and Terry McLaurin's questionable tags cost him one, because Metcalf and Meyers exist. Grant's tight end spot is Juwan Johnson or nothing with Goedert doubtful.

copies.headline: Peter's 4-0 Is Paperwork, Adam's Is Real
copies.body:
Both teams are unbeaten, only one earned it. Adam is 152.7 a week and 40-4 on all-play; Peter is 125.3 and 27-17, with +1.5 wins of luck propping up the record and a 98.1 clunker already on the ledger. The gap lives at receiver. Adam's top three — Jaxon Smith-Njigba in a 46.5 division game, Chris Olave, Rome Odunze — project 48 to Peter's 39, and Peter's depth is a mess: A.J. Brown is on IR, Tee Higgins is questionable, and Denzel Boston's Browns are underdogs in a 39.5 total, the lowest on the board. Quentin Johnston as the fallback is not a plan.
Peter's path is Bijan Robinson plus Kyle Monangai outrunning a 10-point RB edge, and Bijan against Baltimore in a 43.5 total isn't a blowup spot. Meanwhile Aaron Rodgers at 16 has to beat Jayden Daniels, and even if Daniels sits, Brock Purdy in Seattle is a soft landing. Sam LaPorta in Detroit-Arizona (54.5, highest total of the week) is the kind of tiebreaker Peter doesn't have an answer for with Tucker Kraft.

copies.headline: Logan's Questionable Tags Meet Mitchell's Only Star
copies.body:
Mitchell wins this at running back and it isn't especially close. Jahmyr Gibbs is projected for 27 in Detroit's 54.5-total trip to Arizona, the highest-scoring game on the board, and Logan's counter is Jeremiyah Love at 15 with a questionable tag and Emanuel Wilson at 14 behind him. Saquon Barkley is sitting there at zero, which means Logan's entire backfield is depth masquerading as a position group. Philadelphia as a seven-point road underdog in a 42.5-point game also caps Jalen Hurts, and Hurts is already the smaller QB number against Dak Prescott, who gets Tampa at home favored by 8.5 in a 47.5.
The receivers are a coin flip on paper — 42 to 40 — but Logan's number depends on Justin Jefferson being healthy in a 42.5-total game at New Orleans, with Tetairoa McMillan and Xavier Worthy at zero behind him. Mitchell has Nico Collins, Matthew Golden and Courtland Sutton without needing a prayer. Logan is 0-4 and scoring 104.8, tenth in the league. That's not all luck.

copies.headline: Christian's 1-3 Lie Meets Leif's Lunchbox
copies.body:
The records are fiction. Christian is 1-3 with the second-best scoring average in the league and a 29-15 all-play, which means he's been beaten by schedule, not by football, and he's riding 157.5 into this one. The positional math is tight everywhere except tight end, where George Kittle in a 46.5-total game at Seattle is worth six over Dalton Schultz grinding through a 37.5-total in Tennessee — the lowest number on the board. Receiver is the quieter edge: CeeDee Lamb against Tampa with Dallas laying 8.5 in a 47.5 is the single most reliable target share in the game, and Christian still has Deebo, Jameson Williams and Shakir behind him. DeVonta Smith questionable barely dents it.
Leif's path is Josh Allen in Los Angeles, and it's a real one — 54.5 is the highest total of the week and Buffalo is getting three, which is the shape of a quarterback throwing 45 times. McCaffrey and Henry are both road dogs, though, and Henry's workload shrinks if Baltimore trails Atlanta. Christian's back room is deeper than it looks: Aaron Jones, Chase Brown and Tuten all project 14-plus. Leif needs the shootout to carry him. It probably isn't enough.

intro: Adam and Peter are the only unbeatens left, and one of them won't be by Sunday night — Adam gets the slight edge on the road, but this is the kind of game where a single busted blocking assignment on a goal-line carry decides who sits alone at the top. The clearest mismatch is Christian at Leif, where Christian's edge at the skill spots is big enough that Leif would need a career afternoon from somebody who hasn't had one yet. Elsewhere, Noah is favored and still 0-4, which is the most Noah sentence anyone has written this season.
